statements.subject: session
statements.description: A session that will contain mail transactions MUST first be initialized by the use of the EHLO command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A session initialized by the EHLO command with no open mail transaction. There may be zero or more transactions in a session.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: MAIL (or SEND, SOML, or SAML) MUST NOT be sent if a mail transaction is already open.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A session that will contain mail transactions MUST first be initialized by the use of the EHLO command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An EHLO command MAY be issued by a client later in the session. If it is issued after the session begins and the EHLO command is acceptable to the SMTP server, the SMTP server MUST clear all buffers and reset the state exactly as if a RSET command had been issued.
actions: reset state as if RSET issued

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An EHLO command MAY be issued by a client later in the session. If it is issued after the session begins and the EHLO command is acceptable to the SMTP server, the SMTP server MUST clear all buffers and reset the state exactly as if a RSET command had been issued. A mail transaction may be aborted by the RSET, a new EHLO, or the QUIT command.
actions: reset state as if RSET issued

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the EHLO command is not acceptable to the SMTP server, 501, 500, 502, or 550 failure replies MUST be returned as appropriate. The SMTP server MUST stay in the same state after transmitting these replies that it was in before the EHLO was received.
actions: return 501 or 500 or 502 or 550 failure reply

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The MAIL command begins a mail transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A mail transaction may be aborted by the RSET, a new EHLO, or the QUIT command.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: MAIL MUST NOT be sent if a mail transaction is already open, i.e., it should be sent only if ... the previous one successfully concluded with a successful DATA command.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the transaction beginning command argument is not acceptable, a 501 failure reply MUST be returned and the SMTP server MUST stay in the same state.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the commands in a transaction are out of order to the degree that they cannot be processed by the server, a 503 failure reply MUST be returned and the SMTP server MUST stay in the same state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The last command in a session MUST be the QUIT command. The QUIT command SHOULD be used by the client SMTP to request connection closure, even when no session opening command was sent and accepted.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: MAIL (or SEND, SOML, or SAML) MUST NOT be sent if a mail transaction is already open, i.e., it should be sent only if no mail transaction had been started in the session, or if the previous one successfully concluded with a successful DATA command, or if the previous one was aborted.
statements.guard_semantics: MAIL MUST NOT be issued when transaction.open = true

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Once started, a mail transaction consists of a transaction beginning command, one or more RCPT commands, and a DATA command, in that order.
statements.guard_semantics: transaction.command_sequence must follow order: MAIL, RCPT+, DATA

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The NOOP, HELP, EXPN, VRFY, and RSET commands can be used at any time during a session, or without previously initializing a session. SMTP servers SHOULD process these normally (that is, not return a 503 code) even if no EHLO command has yet been received.
statements.trigger: NOOP or HELP or EXPN or VRFY or RSET
